prompt.adult: Paul’s letter is addressed to Philemon, but 1:2 names others too: Apphia, Archippus, and whom?
prompt.child: Paul wrote this letter to Philemon, Apphia, and Archippus. Who else did he write it to?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:2: to Apphia, Archippus, “and to” whom?
prompt.older: According to Philemon 1:2, who else is addressed besides Apphia and Archippus?

verses.text: to the beloved Apphia, Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house:

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 2.
explanation.teen: 1:2 names two people and then one more address. Read the last.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:1 calls Philemon a beloved friend and fellow laborer. 1:3 sends grace and peace from God our Father.
teaching.takeaway: Paul also wrote to “the church in your house.”

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Paul thanks God for Philemon in his prayers (1:4). According to 1:5, Philemon’s love and faith are toward the Lord Jesus and toward whom?
prompt.child: Paul heard about Philemon’s love and faith toward Jesus. Toward whom else?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:5: love and faith toward the Lord Jesus “and” toward whom?
prompt.older: According to Philemon 1:5, toward whom besides the Lord Jesus is Philemon’s love and faith directed?

verses.text: I thank my God, making mention of you always in my prayers,
hearing of your love and faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 5.
explanation.teen: 1:5 names two directions for Philemon’s love and faith. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “toward the Lord Jesus and” in 1:5.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:4 says Paul makes mention of him always in his prayers. 1:6 speaks of the sharing of his faith.
teaching.takeaway: His love and faith are toward all the saints.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Colossians 4:7-9 says Tychicus is coming with Onesimus. How does 4:9 describe Onesimus in relation to the Colossians?
prompt.child: Paul sent Onesimus back with Tychicus. What does Paul say about Onesimus and the people Paul was writing to?
prompt.teen: Colossians 4:9: Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, “who is” what?
prompt.older: According to Colossians 4:9, how is Onesimus connected to the readers?

verses.text: Tychicus, a beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will tell you all the news about me.
with Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all things which are happening here.

explanation.child: Look right after “a faithful and beloved brother,” in verse 9.
explanation.teen: 4:7 describes Tychicus; 4:9 gives Onesimus two titles and then one more phrase. Read it.
explanation.older: It follows “a faithful and beloved brother,” in 4:9.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:8 says Tychicus is sent so he may know their circumstances. 4:9 says they will make known what is happening here.
teaching.takeaway: Onesimus is a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 1:8 Paul says he might be bold enough to command Philemon. Yet in 1:14 he wants to do nothing without Philemon’s consent. How does he want Philemon’s good deed to be?
prompt.child: Paul could have ordered Philemon what to do, but he didn’t. How did Paul want Philemon’s good deed to be done?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:14: “that your good deed might not be by compulsion, as it were, but” what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:8, how does 1:14 say Paul wants Philemon’s good deed to be?

verses.text: Therefore, though I might be very bold in Christ to command you what is fitting,
But without your consent I wanted to do nothing, that your good deed might not be by compulsion, as it were, but voluntary.

explanation.child: Look at the last word of verse 14.
explanation.teen: 1:8 is about commanding; 1:14 contrasts two ways a deed might be done. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “by compulsion, as it were, but” in 1:14.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:9 says Paul rather appeals for love’s sake. 1:13 says he wished to keep Onesimus with him.
teaching.takeaway: Paul wanted Philemon’s good deed to be voluntary.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Paul prays in 1:6 that the sharing of Philemon’s faith may become effective. In 1:21, writing with confidence in his obedience, what does Paul say he knows Philemon will do?
prompt.child: Paul trusted Philemon to obey his request. What did Paul know Philemon would do?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:21: “knowing that you will do” what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:6, what does 1:21 say Paul knows Philemon will do?

verses.text: that the sharing of your faith may become effective by the acknowledgment of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
Having confidence in your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 21.
explanation.teen: 1:6 is a prayer; 1:21 voices confidence and then what Paul knows. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “knowing that you will do” in 1:21.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:22 asks Philemon to prepare a guest room. 1:20 asks him to refresh Paul in the Lord.
teaching.takeaway: Paul knows Philemon will do “even more than I say.”

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Philemon 1:15 suggests Onesimus departed for a while so Philemon might receive him forever. In 1:18, what does Paul say to do if Onesimus has wronged Philemon or owes anything?
prompt.child: Paul said that if Onesimus owed Philemon anything, Philemon should do something. What?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:18: “if he has wronged you or owes anything,” what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:15, what does 1:18 tell Philemon to do with any debt?

choices.text: write it off as a gift

verses.text: For perhaps he departed for a while for this purpose, that you might receive him forever,
But if he has wronged you or owes anything, put that on my account.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 18.
explanation.teen: 1:15 is about receiving; 1:18 gives a condition and then Paul’s instruction. Read the instruction.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:17 asks Philemon to count Paul as a partner. 1:12 says Paul is sending him back.
teaching.takeaway: Paul says, “put that on my account.”

prompt.adult: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus in 1:1. In 1:13, why does he say he wished to keep Onesimus with him on Philemon’s behalf?
prompt.child: Paul wrote this letter to Philemon. Why did he want to keep Onesimus with him?
prompt.teen: Philemon 1:13: Paul wished to keep him so that “on your behalf he might” do what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:1, why does 1:13 say Paul wished to keep Onesimus?

choices.text: carry my letters to the churches
minister to me in my chains

verses.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved friend and fellow laborer,
whom I wished to keep with me, that on your behalf he might minister to me in my chains for the gospel.

explanation.child: Look at the second half of verse 13.
explanation.teen: 1:1 gives Paul’s situation; 1:13 gives a wish and its purpose. Read the purpose.
explanation.older: It follows “on your behalf he might” in 1:13.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:10 calls Onesimus Paul’s son. 1:12 says Paul is sending him back.
teaching.takeaway: Paul wished that Onesimus might “minister to me in my chains.”

prompt.adult: In 1:7 Paul rejoices that Philemon has refreshed others. In 1:12, as he sends Onesimus back, how does Paul describe him?
prompt.child: Paul sent Onesimus back to Philemon. What did Paul call Onesimus?
prompt.older: Read with 1:4, what does Paul call Onesimus in 1:12?

verses.text: I thank my God, making mention of you always in my prayers,
I am sending him back. You therefore receive him, that is, my own heart,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 12.
explanation.teen: 1:4 is Paul’s thanks in prayer; 1:12 sends Onesimus back and then describes him. Read the description.
explanation.older: It follows “receive him, that is,” in 1:12.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:10 says Paul appeals for Onesimus. 1:20 asks Philemon to refresh Paul in the Lord.
